_note: The station's residents (orbit_npcs.py): characters who are not players. Every line is English, {"en": ...} (a list of variants for greetings, topics and cases). Schedules are station time (UTC): [hour, room], a room of null meaning off duty. Topics may take live values ("live": a provider in orbit_npcs.py) and "cases" (other lines for what the provider found). "min" is the affinity a topic or favour needs. See README.md.

desc.en: A broad man in a patterned apron with a towel over one shoulder, who laughs with his whole chest. He knows everyone's usual order, and most of their news.

en: Welcome to the Cantina! Sit anywhere that's bolted down.
Ah, a thirsty face. What can I do for you?
Come in, come in. The jukebox is stuck on swing tonight, sorry.
{name}! The usual, or are we feeling brave today?
Look who's back. Good to see you, {name}.
{name}, my friend! Your stool's still warm.
There's my favourite regular. Sit, sit, {name}.
Ha! That one's beyond me. Ask me about gossip instead, I know plenty.
Hmm, never heard of it, and I hear everything in here.

idle.en: {npc} polishes a glass until it squeaks.
{npc} hums along with the jukebox, a little off key.
Iced coffee, anyone? Fresh palm sugar today.
They say prices on the Moon are wild this week. Don't quote me.
{npc} slides a cup along the bar to nobody in particular, then catches it himself.
Try the Orbit Special. Nobody knows what's in it, not even me.
{npc} feeds the jukebox a coin and picks something slow.
{npc} slides a mug of hot chocolate down the bar to someone who looks like they need it.
Whoever keeps picking Both on the jukebox: I know it's you.

en: Quiet days lately. Even the gossip is taking a nap.
Have you heard? {a} and {b} were married at {place}. The whole station's still talking about it.
Big news: {a} and {b} are getting married at {place}, {day} at {hour}. Bring flowers!
Between you and me, {rich} has more credits than the bank on the Moon. Rich people tip badly, you know.
The crew {crew} is top of the board. Their captain drinks nothing but water. Suspicious, if you ask me.
{miner} has dug up more ore than anyone. Comes in here covered in dust, every time.
{n} people are about on the station right now, {names} among them.
Just you and me right now. Cosy, isn't it?
My iced coffee has palm sugar and a secret. The secret is more palm sugar. Fifteen credits, and you earn XP faster for ten minutes.
Prices are behaving themselves today. Boring, but good for the heart.
Word at the bar is that {good} is dear right now: {price} credits {where}. Sell, sell, sell. You didn't hear it from me.
Word at the bar is that {good} is cheap right now: {price} credits {where}. Buy low, my friend.
Swing or synthwave. Somebody once pressed both, and the station's gravity wobbled. True story. Probably.
Nothing on at the moment. Why not throw a party in your cabin?
Right now it's {event}, for another {time}. Go on, don't miss it.
Nothing on right now. Next up is {event}, {day} at {hour}.
Alright, for you. The time capsule below the old pump room isn't a legend. Bring a light, and a key made of brass.
New on the menu: hot chocolate with a marshmallow, ginger fizz, instant noodles, and the Orbit Special. Don't ask what's in the Special. Type list.
The hot chocolate is my grandmother's recipe. The ginger fizz is nobody's fault.
There's a pond past the Sky Park, north: Willow Nook. Hana feeds the fish. Catch a trout and the Spice Market will pay you for it.

ask.en: My chilli sauce jar is empty, and that's a crisis. Bring me three bags of chillies from the farm, would you?

thanks.en: Chillies! You've saved the Cantina. Here, for your trouble.

desc.en: A wiry old man in grease-stained coveralls, reading glasses pushed up into grey hair. He talks to the reactor as if it were an old friend, and it seems to listen.

en: Mind the pipes. What do you need?
Hm? Oh, a visitor. Don't touch anything that hums.
Welcome to Engineering. Loud, hot, and the best room on the station.
Ah, {name}. Come to help an old man?
{name}. Good. I have work, if you have hands.
{name}! Pull up a crate. The reactor's in a good mood today.
My favourite pair of hands. Hello, {name}.
I fix reactors, not riddles. Ask me about the reactor, or about work.
Can't help you there. Ask me something with bolts in it.

idle.en: {npc} taps a pipe with a spanner and listens, frowning.
Easy, girl. Easy. Nobody's rushing you.
{npc} mutters numbers under his breath and scribbles them on his palm.
Forty years on this station, and she still surprises me.
{npc} taps a gauge with one knuckle, listens, and nods.
The Crew Lounge kettle is older than half the crew. Still boils faster than mine.

en: When she drifts out of tune, you play her tones back to her: low on the left, high on the right. Engineers get paid for it, and she gets calm.
When I came up, this was three modules and a coffee machine. Now look at it: a mall, a casino, a Gate to other worlds. I still miss the coffee machine.
You're level {level}, a {rank}. {need} more XP and you'll be level {next}. Keep your hands busy.
Level {level}, a {rank}. There's nothing left I can teach you. Go and teach someone else.
A crew keycard at level two, an officer's at ten, and engineers get a technician's card at three for the Reactor Core. Doors on this station respect experience.
My daughter pilots ferries between Glasir and Karmina now. She sends me a postcard from every port. I keep them in my toolbox, next to the good spanner.
The Crew Lounge is west of the Crew Quarters. Sofa, kettle, a puzzle of the Earth nobody can finish. The last piece is somewhere. I have my suspicions about the cleaning bot.

ask.en: The pump housings need patching. Bring me three pieces of scrap metal from the Debris Field, outside the hull. Suit up first.

thanks.en: Good scrap. Good hands. Here, you earned this.

ask.en: The console's memory is failing. Two old circuit boards from the Debris Field would do. Don't tell the captain.

thanks.en: Perfect. She'll remember her tones for another year.

ask.en: This one's between us. The station's old satellite needs a new chip, and I only trust you to find one. A satellite chip, from the Debris Field.

thanks.en: You found one! Now the old bird can sing again. Thank you, truly.

role.en: keeper of the Way of Starlight

desc.en: A calm woman in a long indigo shawl stitched with tiny silver stars. She tends the lanterns one by one, and her voice never rises above a gentle murmur.

en: Welcome under the dome. Stay as long as you like.
May your light hold steady, traveller.
Hello. Speak softly; the dome listens.
{name}, welcome back. Your lantern from last time still glows.
Ah, {name}. The stars are clear today.
{name}, dear friend. Sit with me a while.
I know your steps by now, {name}. Welcome.
That I cannot answer. Some questions are for the stars, and they are slow to reply.
I don't know, and that is alright. Staying curious is one of the three things.

idle.en: {npc} trims the wick of a lantern and sets it back in the alcove.
{npc} sits on a bench and looks up at the dome in silence.
Every lantern here is a promise someone means to keep.
{npc} brushes a speck of dust from the bronze bell.
{npc} straightens a lantern in its alcove and whispers a name to it.
Sit a while, if you like. The benches here were made for slow evenings.

en: The Way asks only three things: keep your word, stay curious, and look after one another. The rest is lanterns, and a bell, and good company.
{n} lanterns have been lit here today. Light one for a promise, three credits, and I'll keep it glowing.
It's the Lantern Festival! {n} of {goal} lanterns are lit. When we reach {goal}, the whole station shares a gift.
The festival's goal is reached: {n} lanterns glow tonight. What a sight.
The Lantern Festival comes on the hundredth day of the year, {day}. Lanterns are free that day, and together we try to light {goal}.
The Lantern Festival is today! {n} of {goal} lanterns are lit so far. Every lantern is free, and when we reach {goal}, everyone on the station shares a gift.
The festival's goal was reached today: {n} lanterns! Everyone has a gift waiting.
We ring it for those still travelling. It answers with three tones, low, middle and high, one for each of the three things.

In the Starlight rite, two people each light a lantern and bring the two lights together into one. We keep a moment of silence, they speak their own promises, and the star bell rings three times. Celeste at the jeweller's books the halls.
When a little one joins a family, bring them here. We light a lantern for them, I speak their name under the dome, and the bell rings once, so the stars learn it too. Say naming rite, and the name.
On the longest crossing, one of them fell asleep on her watch. The others didn't wake her. They kept her watch for her, in turns, until morning. That, more than any rule, is the Way.

role.en: a traveller who comes only at night

desc.en: Someone in a dusty travelling cloak, hood half up, leaning on the rail as if they had been there for years. Their boots carry red dust, blue ice and moss all at once.

appear.en: A figure in a dusty cloak is suddenly at the rail, as if the night brought them.

vanish.en: When you look again, the traveller in the dusty cloak is gone.

en: Ah. Another one who can't sleep.
The Earth turns, and here you are. Hello.
Shh. Listen. The stars are loud tonight.
{name}. You came back. They always come back.
Good evening, {name}. Or morning. Up here it's hard to say.
{name}, my fellow night owl. Stand here; the view is better.
I saved you a place at the rail, {name}.
Some doors I won't open for you. You'll have to find the handles yourself.
Hm. The answer to that is further away than Glasir.

idle.en: {npc} traces a constellation on the glass with one finger.
Every world has its own silence. This one hums.
{npc} checks an old compass that doesn't seem to point north.
Somewhere out there, a note is waiting to be found.
Out there, past the Gate, the ships wait their turn like birds on a wire.
{npc} traces a constellation on the glass with one finger.

en: No song is being sought right now. Rest your ears. They will be needed.
You found every note already. I heard it; the whole sky did.
You carry {have} of {total} notes. The next one is closer than you think: this world, not another. Look where people pass without looking.
You carry {have} of {total} notes. The next one isn't on this world. Pack for a journey, and a different kind of air.
Sailors on your Earth once steered by these same stars. Up here we steer by them still, only nobody admits it.
Evergrove's moss, Glasir's ice, Karmina's red dust, all in my boots. The Drift Bazaar sells everything except a map to where you really want to go.
A traveller. Like you, only longer. Soren is the name I travel under, and it has never once asked me to stay.
It's {time} by the station's clock, {part}. The Earth doesn't care; it spins anyway.
The founder of this simulation hid more than notes. She hid a habit: every riddle, she wrote at night. Think like someone who can't sleep.
East of the Gate Hall there's a gallery with telescopes. Look through the one marked Evergrove: it only ever shows clouds shaped like dragons. I've watched for hours.

desc.en: A young man with safety goggles on his forehead and three screwdrivers in his shirt pocket, who demonstrates every device by nearly breaking it.

en: Welcome to Gearworks! Everything here beeps, blinks or drills.
Looking for something shiny? Or useful? Ideally both.
Hi! Don't mind the smoke, it's a feature.
Ah, {name}, my best customer. Well, one of them.
{name}! For you, the friends' price, as always.
No idea, but I could probably build a device that knows. Ask me about gear.
That's not in my catalogue. Try drills, suits or mappers.

idle.en: {npc} tightens a tiny screw on a scanner and holds it up to the light.
Plasma drills! Twenty percent faster, zero percent safer. Kidding. Mostly.
{npc} tests a headlamp by shining it in his own eyes, and regrets it.
{npc} spins a drill bit on his fingertip and catches it without looking.

en: Today's special is the {thing}, just {price} credits. I'd buy two, but I already own four.
No special today. Everything's special, really.
A steel drill strikes every twenty seconds, a plasma drill every sixteen. The rocks at the Belt won't know what hit them.
The EVA suit gives you three minutes of air outside, an oxygen tank three more. Listen for the warnings, and if you run out, the tow drone brings you back for a small fee.
A pocket mapper remembers every room you've walked. A holo mapper knows every public room, even the ones you haven't been brave enough to visit.
Every job has its tools: a torque wrench for engineers, a nav computer for pilots, a market terminal for traders. The better ones raise your pay by a fifth.

desc.en: A cheerful woman with a cat asleep on her shoulder and a tiny robot riding in her apron pocket. There is fur on her sleeves and oil on her fingers, and she doesn't mind either.

en: Hello! Mind your step, someone's napping on the floor.
Welcome to Whiskers & Widgets! Everyone here is looking for a home.
Hi there! Would you like to meet somebody?
Welcome back, {name}. The kittens remember you.
{name}! Come, come, there's a new jellyfish who wants to say hello.
I only know animals and robots, and some of the robots think they're animals. Ask me about pets.
Hmm, that's beyond me. Ask me about care, or tricks.

idle.en: {npc} scratches a sleepy cat behind the ears.
Who's a good robot? You are. Yes, you are.
{npc} tops up the glow jellyfish's tank with sparkling water.
The robot in {npc}'s pocket beeps; she beeps back.
{npc} rolls a ball of yarn across the floor for a robot cat, who ignores it grandly.

en: We have a little robot, an orange space cat, a robot cat, a space fox, a glow jellyfish and a mini drone. Some wild ones turn up out on the worlds, too, if you're lucky.

Feed them pet food or treats, play with them, and let them rest. They get hungry and bored slowly, in real time. A lonely pet goes quiet, but it never stops loving you, and a little play always cheers it up.
Once your pet is a bit older, teach it tricks: teach trick, and the trick's name. A few good lessons, when it's happy and rested, and it'll show off for everyone.
{pet} is alright, but could use a little more attention. Some play, maybe a treat?
You don't have a pet yet! Have a look around; someone here might choose you.
{pet} looks wonderful: bright eyes, full belly. You're doing everything right.
Oh, {pet} seems a little sad and quiet. Nothing a meal, some play and a nap can't fix. They always forgive.

ask.en: The glow jellyfish love moonpetals from Evergrove, but I can never get away from the shop. Could you bring me a basket?

thanks.en: Look how they glow! Thank you. Here, a treat for your own little one.

desc.en: An elegant woman in a long silver-grey jacket, a jeweller's loupe on a chain around her neck. She speaks precisely, smiles often, and remembers the ring size of everyone she has ever met.

en: Welcome to Starglint Jewellers. Rings, and everything that comes after them.
Good day! Browsing, or planning something special?
Hello, hello. Mind the display cases, they're older than me.
{name}, lovely to see you. What can I polish for you today?
{name}, my dear! Tea? I always have tea for friends.
{name}! I was just thinking about you.
Ah, I only know rings and weddings, I'm afraid. Ask me about those.
That I couldn't say. Rings, venues and ceremonies, those I know.

idle.en: {npc} polishes a ring and holds it up to the light, satisfied.
Every ring is a small promise you can wear.
{npc} checks a leather-bound booking book and hums.
The Jasmine Pavilion is lovely in the evening, just so you know.
{npc} polishes a ring until the stars in it seem to move.

en: A silver band, a gold band, or a star-crystal ring for someone who deserves the sky. Buy one, find your person, and say propose to, and their name, when you're both in the same room.
Once you're engaged, book here: book wedding, the hall, the tier, the ceremony and the time, for example book wedding pavilion grand neutral 14:00, in station time. Then invite your guests.
Three halls: the Star Dome Hall under the glass, the Jasmine Pavilion in the garden, and the castle's Great Hall in Evergrove, with a fire big enough to roast a cart. Each takes one wedding an hour.

Simple is {simple} credits: flowers and soft music. Grand is {grand}: garlands, lights and a string trio. Luxurious is {lux}: all of that, a hall full of crystal lanterns, and fireworks for the whole station.
Two kinds. The Starlight rite, with Amara, lanterns and the star bell. Or a neutral ceremony with me: your vows, your yes, and your signatures in the station's register.
My book is empty for now. Somebody should fix that.
Next in my book: {a} and {b}, at {place}, {day} at {hour}.

desc.en: A sunburnt man in a faded captain's cap, who counts the minutes to departure out loud and has never once missed one.

en: All aboard who's going aboard! Oh, you're just saying hello. Hello!
Welcome to the Dock. Mind the clamps.
The Starling leaves every two minutes, rain or shine. Not that it rains.
{name}, my favourite passenger! The window seat is yours.
Ahoy, {name}! Sit up front with me next time.
I know routes, not riddles. Ask me about the ferry or the worlds.
Couldn't tell you. But I could fly you somewhere that knows.

idle.en: Ferry to the Moon, Karmina, Glasir and beyond! Leaving soon!
{npc} checks his pocket watch, then the schedule board, then his watch again.
{npc} gives the Wombat's hull a friendly pat.
Two minutes between departures. You could set a clock by us. Some people do.
The ferry's never late. The universe is sometimes early.

en: The Starling leaves in {time}. It's slow but cheap: five credits and three a unit of distance. Say ferry to, and a world.

The Moon's close, Glasir's the far end. Karmina's red and dusty, Evergrove's green and a bit magical, Lumina never sleeps, and Pixel Pier is one big arcade. The Drift Bazaar has no customs, if you catch my meaning.
Customs search the Gate most, the ferry less, private ships least. If you're carrying something without a label, don't tell me about it.
The little Wombat flies miners to the Asteroid Belt for five credits. Pilots ride free, professional courtesy.

ask.en: The Starling's water tank is running low, and comet ice is the best water there is. Three blocks from the Belt or Glasir?

thanks.en: Beautiful ice. The passengers thank you, and so do I.

role.en: a curious girl who lives on the station

desc.en: A girl of about nine with a scraped knee, a backpack covered in planet stickers, and a notebook full of questions. She writes down every answer she gets, even the silly ones.

en: Hi! Do you know why the Earth doesn't fall down? I'm still working on it.
Hello! Can I ask you a question? Just one. Maybe three.
Oh! A grown-up! Are you an astronaut? Everyone here is, kind of.
{name}! I wrote down what you told me last time!
Hi, {name}! I have a new question for you.
{name}! You're my favourite grown-up. Don't tell the others.
{name}! Look, I drew you a rocket!
I don't know that one either! Let's both find out, okay?
Hmm, I'll write it in my notebook and ask my teacher.

idle.en: Why is space black if the sun is so bright? Anybody?
{npc} scribbles something in her notebook, tongue sticking out in concentration.
{npc} hops from one floor tile to the next, avoiding the lines.
Stuffed pancakes are the best food in the galaxy. I checked.
Look! I can see Grandma's island from here! Hi, Grandma!
{npc} asks the librarian robot a question, and it beeps back a very long answer.
{npc} reads the field guide under the lamp, lips moving.
This book says never answer a puffcap's riddle with a potato. Why would anybody do that?
{npc} rolls down the lawn and gets grass all over her backpack.

en: Okay: if you sneeze in zero gravity, do you fly backwards? I think yes.
Do the fish on the station know they're in space?
If the Moon had a shop, what would it sell? I think cheese. Felix says helium.
School is in the Archive in the mornings. The librarian robot is our teacher. It never gets tired of questions, which is lucky.
Did you know the station goes round the Earth every hour and a half? That's sixteen sunrises a day! I've only seen four, then I fell asleep.
I want a space fox so badly. Priya says I have to be responsible first. I fed the Cantina's robot barista once. It didn't eat.
The best score at Pixel Pier is {name}'s: {score} at {game}! One day that'll be me.
Nobody's got a high score at Pixel Pier yet! I'll be first. After my homework.
Okay, a secret: Oskar talks to the reactor, and I think the reactor talks back. Don't tell.
The Reading Room is behind the Archive, west. My favourite is the field guide. You can read the poems too, and there's a swap shelf: put something on it and someone finds it!

role.en: a trader who sells things without labels

desc.en: A woman in a long charcoal coat with too many pockets, leaning where the light doesn't quite reach. People call her Shade. She has never said whether that is her name.

en: You found the alley. Most people walk past it.
Keep your voice down. What do you want?
Buying or selling? I don't do chatting. Much.
Back already, {name}? The goods haven't changed. The prices have.
{name}. For you, I'll even smile. There.
I don't sell answers to that.

idle.en: {npc} counts something in a pocket without taking it out.
No labels, no questions, no refunds.
{npc} glances at the mouth of the alley, then back into the shadows.
Everything's for sale here. Even quiet. Especially quiet.

en: Today a {good} goes for {price} credits here. In Lumina's Night Market they pay a lot more. The trip between is your business.
The Gate's scanners are nosy. The ferry's less so. A ship of your own with a scanner bay, hardly at all. And the Bazaar, Evergrove and the Belt never check. I didn't tell you that.
Shade is what they call me. A shadow doesn't need a name; it needs a wall to lean on.
Lumina City's Night Market buys what I sell, no questions asked. Take it there, and mind the customs on the way.
A secret, for a friend: the customs officers at Pixel Pier only check half the travellers. They'd rather be playing games.

role.en: the host of the Tournament Stage

desc.en: A lanky young man in a jacket covered in pixel badges, holding a microphone that isn't plugged into anything. He announces everything, including his own sandwiches.

en: Welcome, challenger, to the Tournament Stage!
Ooh, a new face in the spotlight! Hello!
Ladies, gentlemen, and robots: it's you!
{name} returns to the stage! The crowd goes wild! The crowd is me.
{name}, my friend, the spotlight missed you.
That's not in the rulebook, friend. Ask me about duels or high scores!
I only announce, I don't explain. Ask about the arcade!

idle.en: Who will be the fastest hand on Pixel Pier? Step up!
{npc} taps his unplugged microphone. Nothing happens. He nods, satisfied.
Remember: draw means draw. Not almost draw. Draw.
Who's brave enough for a duel? The big chairs are warm and waiting!

en: The fastest hand on the board is {name}, with {won} duels won. Challenge someone here: duel, and their name.
Nobody has won a duel yet! Be the first: duel, and a name.
The record I'm proudest of: {name}, {score} at {game}. Can you beat it? Cabinet Row, west of the Hall.
No records yet! Cabinet Row, west of the Hall, is waiting for a hero.
No tournament on the calendar. Ask an admin to start one!
The tournament is on, for another {time}! {leader} leads with {points} wins. Duel here to climb!
The tournament is on, for another {time}, and nobody has won a duel yet! Step up!
Next tournament: {day} at {hour}, station time, right here. The most duels won takes the prize.
Tokens at the machine on Cabinet Row, five credits each. Good games print tickets, and the Prize Counter east of the Hall swaps them for prizes.

desc.en: A stocky man with forearms like mooring ropes and a laugh like a cargo door. His overalls say GINO in fading marker.

en: Oi! Mind your toes, crate coming through.
Hello there! Busy day, busy day.
{name}, my friend! Come, sit a minute.
{name}! The best face on the station, after mine.
Ha, you're asking the wrong man. I lift boxes.
No idea! Ask me about crates, I know crates.

idle.en: {npc} heaves a crate onto a trolley with a grunt.
Clamps on! Who left the airlock humming?
{npc} eats a stuffed pancake in four enormous bites.
Best lunch break on the station, this.
{npc} stacks crates into a perfect tower, then admires it.
Rocco! One more iced coffee, and put it on my tab.
{npc} tells a story about a runaway crate to anyone who'll listen.
{npc} stretches his back and groans happily.
The ramen at the Food Court, the one with the egg in it: that's why I work so hard.
{npc} sits on an upturned crate and eats a sesame bun in three bites.

en: Mornings at the Dock, lunch at the Food Court, afternoons in the Cargo Bay, and evenings at the Cantina, where the real work is resting.
Twenty years up here. I can tell the time by which pump is humming. Wouldn't live anywhere else.
Space ramen, the one in a bowl with a straw. The egg floats around in there like a little moon. Then a fruit skewer, for health.

desc.en: A young woman with soil under her nails, a sun hat she wears indoors out of habit, and a watering can she never quite puts down.

en: Hello! Mind the seedlings, they're shy.
Oh, hi! Isn't it green in here?
{name}! I saved you a strawberry. Well, I ate it. But I saved you the thought.
I only know plants, sorry. Ask me about farming!
No idea! But I know when a chilli is ripe.

idle.en: {npc} waters a row of chillies, one plant at a time.
Water once, and the crop gives a little more. Plants like attention, like people.
{npc} kneels by a flower bed and talks quietly to the tulips.
{npc} threads fresh jasmine buds into a long string for the pavilion's roof.
The jasmine opens slowly all day. Weddings here smell wonderful.
A cold iced coffee after a day in the garden. Perfect.
{npc} brushes soil off her hands.
{npc} scatters a handful of fish food on the pond, and the water boils with perch.
If a golden koi bites, let it go. It's bad luck to keep it, and worse manners.
{npc} sits under the willow and hums to the fish.

en: Buy seeds at the rack, plant, water once, and harvest when it's ripe. Water spinach in ten minutes, moon melon in a day. Patience grows the best ones.
I thread the pavilion's jasmine every morning. For weddings, I thread twice as much.
Cast, wait for the tug, then reel, quick! Perch are easy, carp are heavy, and trout are clever. The golden koi is to be let go; she's older than the station's second deck.
The Spice Market buys perch, carp and trout. Not the koi. Never the koi.

ask.en: The old gardeners say a frost pearl's cold wakes up sleepy seeds. Could you bring me one from Glasir?

thanks.en: It's so cold! The seeds will love it. Here, a packet of vanilla seeds for you.

desc.en: A tiny old woman with a walking stick grown, not carved, from a living branch. Moss sprites follow her about like ducklings.

en: Welcome to Mossbrook, dear. Wipe your boots on the moss.
Ah, a traveller. You look hungry. Everyone looks hungry to me.
{name}, dear! Back in the green again.
There you are, {name}. The sprites asked about you.
{name}! Come, come, the kettle's always on for you.
My favourite traveller. Sit by me, {name}.
Oh, that's a question for younger ears than mine. Ask me about the woods.
I don't know, dear, but the trees might. Ask me about the castle.

idle.en: {npc} shoos a moss sprite off her windowsill, then gives it a crumb.
Mind the puffcaps in the Hollow, they sneeze.
{npc} listens to the trees with her eyes closed.
The Whispering Wood always tells the truth. You just have to be patient.
{npc} warms her hands at the great fire.
{npc} leans on her stick and hums an old tune.
In my day we fished the river with a bent pin and a lot of patience.
{npc} sits on the well's rim and knits something long and green.

en: The moss sprite just wants to be caught. The ember beetle wants to be admired. The bramble bear wants a nap. Face them with a clear head, and nobody gets hurt.
The castle's Great Hall takes weddings now. A fire, long tables, and the stars from the tower. Better than any dome, if you ask me.

ask.en: My porridge wants red quinoa from Karmina, and my knees don't want the journey. Two sacks, dear?

thanks.en: Oh, lovely. Porridge for a week! Take this, dear, and don't argue.
